title: Lamanite armies approach Ammonihah
summary: On the tenth day of the eleventh month of the nineteenth year, Lamanite armies are seen approaching the land of Ammonihah. The city had been rebuilt; Moroni had stationed an army by its borders, and dirt had been cast up around it for protection.
characters: the army stationed by the city's borders
locations: the borders of the rebuilt city

explicit_facts.text: The armies of the Lamanites were seen approaching the land of Ammonihah on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the nineteenth year.
The city had been rebuilt.
Moroni had stationed an army by the borders of the city.
Dirt had been cast up around the city to shield the stationed army from the Lamanites' arrows and stones.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The approaching armies, rebuilt city, stationed army, and cast-up dirt can be shown in one view.
unspecified_visual_details: The city's architecture, terrain, and people's appearances are not specified.

narration.text: the armies of the Lamanites were seen approaching towards the land of Ammonihah.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Moroni as present during the approach; the verse describes his earlier action.
Do not depict the rebuilding or construction of the dirt barrier as happening during the approach.
Do not invent a battle or injuries in this scene.

title: The defenses of Ammonihah
summary: The Lamanites expect partly rebuilt Ammonihah to be easy prey, but its earthen ridge prevents their stones and arrows from taking effect and restricts access to its entrance. Their chief captains are astonished by the Nephites’ preparations.

explicit_facts.text: Ammonihah had been partly rebuilt, and the Lamanites supposed it would be easy prey because they had destroyed it before.
The Nephites had dug a high ridge of earth around them; the Lamanites’ stones and arrows could not take effect, and they could approach only by the entrance.
The Lamanite chief captains were exceedingly astonished by the Nephites’ preparations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The ridge and entrance can be shown from the Lamanite side as the chief captains observe them.
unspecified_visual_details: The captains’ appearances and the ridge’s exact shape are unspecified.

narration.text: the chief captains of the Lamanites were astonished exceedingly, because of the wisdom of the Nephites in preparing their places of security.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earlier destruction or the digging of the ridge as happening now.
Do not invent an attack, dialogue, or additional defenses.

title: The Lamanites prepare for battle
summary: The Lamanites, prepared with shields, breastplates, and thick skin garments, expect to overpower the Nephites. They are astonished by the Nephites’ preparations.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite leaders expect their large numbers to let them attack as before.
The Lamanites have shields, breastplates, and thick garments of skins.
They expect to subject or slay the Nephites.
The Nephites are prepared according to Moroni’s instructions, in a manner unknown among the children of Lehi.
The Lamanites are exceedingly astonished at the Nephites’ preparations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lamanite shields, breastplates, and thick garments can be depicted.
unspecified_visual_details: Clothing, equipment designs, and colors are unspecified.

narration.text: they had also prepared themselves with shields, and with breastplates

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamanites’ expected conquest as an event that occurs.

title: The captains do not attack
summary: Amalickiah does not come down to battle. His chief captains do not dare attack the Nephites at Ammonihah. Moroni had altered the management of affairs among the Nephites. The Lamanites were disappointed in their places of retreat and could not come upon the Nephites.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah did not come down to battle.
His chief captains did not dare attack the Nephites at the city of Ammonihah.
Moroni had altered the management of affairs among the Nephites.
The Lamanites were disappointed in their places of retreat and could not come upon the Nephites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The scene can show no attack taking place at Ammonihah.
unspecified_visual_details: The chief captains' exact location and appearance are unspecified.
Moroni's alterations are not visually described.

narration.text: But behold, Amalickiah did not come down himself to battle.

And behold, his chief captains durst not attack the Nephites at the city of Ammonihah, for Moroni had altered the management of affairs among the Nephites, insomuch that the Lamanites were disappointed in their places of retreat and they could not come upon them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma 49:10 presents Amalickiah leading an attack as a hypothetical possibility, not an event that occurred.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Amalickiah at the battle or assign him a location.
Do not depict the hypothetical attack in Alma 49:10 as an event.
Do not invent a confrontation, dialogue, or specific defensive alterations.

title: The army marches toward Noah
summary: The Lamanites retreat into the wilderness, take their camp, and march toward Noah. Their chief captains swear to destroy its people.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites retreat into the wilderness, take their camp, and march toward Noah.
They do not know Moroni has fortified every city in the land; their chief captains swear to destroy Noah’s people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The army can be shown marching with its camp.
unspecified_visual_details: The camp’s appearance and the captains’ oath-taking gestures are unspecified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent words spoken during the oath.

title: Noah is strongly fortified
summary: The city of Noah, formerly weak, has become stronger than Ammonihah through Moroni’s efforts. An unnamed group marches toward Noah to battle, as Moroni had anticipated.

explicit_facts.text: The city of Noah had been weak but became stronger than the city Ammonihah through Moroni’s efforts.
Moroni supposed the group would be frightened at Ammonihah and march to Noah for battle because Noah had been the weakest part of the land.
The group marched toward Noah to battle, according to Moroni’s desires.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The unnamed group may be shown approaching the strengthened city of Noah.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the city and its defenses is not described.
The group’s identities and appearance are not specified.

narration.text: the city of Noah, which had hitherto been a weak place, had now, by the means of Moroni, become strong, yea, even to exceed the strength of the city Ammonihah.
they would march thither to battle; and thus it was according to his desires.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni’s supposition is retrospective explanation, not a separate present-time scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed group from these verses alone.
Do not depict Moroni planning at the same time as the group’s approach.
Do not specify the design of Noah’s defenses as a sourced fact.

title: Lehi commands Noah
summary: Moroni has appointed Lehi chief captain over Noah. The Lamanites learn Lehi commands there, fear him, and bring up their armies.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni appointed Lehi chief captain over the men of Noah.
The Lamanites learn Lehi commands the city and fear him exceedingly; their captains nevertheless bring up their armies.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lehi may be shown with the defenders at Noah as the army approaches.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner in which the Lamanites learn Lehi commands is unspecified.

narration.text: when the Lamanites had found that Lehi commanded the city

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Lehi’s earlier battle in the valley on the east of Sidon.

title: The entrance is defended
summary: The high bank and deep ditch leave the entrance as the only way into the fort. The Nephites are prepared to defend against attempts to enter elsewhere or through the entrance.

explicit_facts.text: The high bank and deep ditch prevent the Lamanites from entering the fort except by its entrance.
The Nephites are prepared to cast stones and arrows at anyone attempting to climb into the fort elsewhere.
A body of their strongest men is prepared with swords and slings to defend the entrance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The entrance, bank, ditch, and prepared Nephite defenders can be shown together.
unspecified_visual_details: The defenders’ number and individual appearances are unspecified.
The fort’s precise design beyond its bank, ditch, and entrance is unspecified.

narration.text: to smite down all who should attempt to come into their place of security by the place of entrance

prohibited_inventions: Do not show an attack or an attempted entry as already underway.
Do not identify the fort’s location by a name absent from these verses.

title: The Lamanites attack the entrance
summary: The Lamanite captains bring their armies to the entrance and try to enter the fort. The Nephites repeatedly drive them back; the attackers suffer immense slaughter.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanite captains bring their armies before the entrance and contend with the Nephites to enter.
The attackers are repeatedly driven back and suffer immense slaughter.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The assault and defenders driving attackers back may be depicted without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific combat choreography is not described.

narration.text: they were driven back from time to time

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict graphic injuries or severed body parts.

title: The attempt to breach the bank fails
summary: Unable to gain the pass, the Lamanites try to dig down the earth banks. Stones and arrows sweep them off instead.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites try to dig down the banks to make a pass for their army.
Stones and arrows sweep them off; the ditches are filled in measure with dead and wounded bodies.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The defenders’ stones and arrows can be shown striking the attacking force without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The bodies and injuries are not described in detail.

narration.text: they began to dig down their banks of earth

prohibited_inventions: Do not graphically depict bodies or wounds.

title: The battle’s outcome
summary: The Lamanite captains are slain, and more than a thousand Lamanites die. No Nephites are slain; about fifty are wounded, protected by their armor and shields.

explicit_facts.text: More than a thousand Lamanites are slain, including all their chief captains; no Nephites are slain.
About fifty Nephites are wounded; shields, breastplates, and head-plates protect them, and many wounds are on their legs.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephite shields and armor may be visible; present the aftermath without graphic injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The positions and appearances of casualties are unspecified.

narration.text: there was not a single soul of the Nephites which was slain

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict blood, wounds, or severed body parts.

title: The Lamanites flee
summary: The Lamanites see their chief captains are slain, flee into the wilderness, and return to Nephi to inform Amalickiah of their loss.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites flee into the wilderness after seeing their chief captains slain.
They return to Nephi to inform Amalickiah, who is a Nephite by birth, of their loss.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fleeing army can be shown moving into the wilderness.
unspecified_visual_details: The reporting to Amalickiah is not shown as a separate moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Amalickiah receiving the report in this scene.

title: Amalickiah’s anger
summary: Amalickiah is exceedingly angry at his people for failing to subject the Nephites. He curses God and Moroni and swears he will drink Moroni’s blood.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah is exceedingly angry because he has not subjected the Nephites.
He curses God and Moroni and swears an oath that he will drink Moroni’s blood.

unspecified_visual_details: Amalickiah’s setting, gestures, and appearance are unspecified.

title: Peace and preaching
summary: The nineteenth year ends. Peace and prosperity continue among the people, as ordained teachers preach the word of God.

explicit_facts.text: The nineteenth year of the reign of the judges ends.
There is continual peace and great prosperity in the church, attributed to heed and diligence toward the word of God.
Helaman, Shiblon, Corianton, Ammon and his brethren, and others ordained to preach teach repentance among the people.
